hot.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
hot.summary: The authors introduce numerically stable replacements for hard- and soft-target cross-entropy that preserve tiny gradients at high confidence and near-equal student–teacher logits. The method computes small differences directly instead of subtracting rounded probabilities. In fp32 squared modular addition modulo 97 without weight decay, fixed loss reaches 85% test accuracy, while standard loss drops from 61% to 23%; this toy result does not establish effects in large-scale training.

hot.title: Agentic World Action Models
hot.summary: AW-0 adds a skill-program stream to a model that predicts future video and actions for language-directed manipulation. The program can guide imagined states and action generation, but is usually a plan conditioning an action expert rather than executable code. Across eight bimanual tasks, AW-0 scores 71.1% on average versus DreamZero’s 46.0%; rubric scores measure partial-credit progress, not full task success.

hot.title: Action Learning for Scientific Simulations
hot.summary: LEAP learns a reusable cost to score trajectories from paths. It contrasts paths with samples from a reference process and combines a path log-ratio with the reference action. On a 31-body orbital benchmark, its model reaches 0.228 NRMSE versus about 1 for local models; molecular tests reuse the action for new requests. These results apply to the tested settings.

hot.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro Tech Blog: Advancing Open Intelligence
hot.summary: Moonshot AI introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro, a post-trained version of Kimi K3 and its most capable 3T-class open-weight model, with a 1M-token context window and a 2-3× faster Highspeed variant. Trained with far more RL compute across hundreds of domains, it matches or approaches leading proprietary models on coding, 3D creation, finance, and agentic benchmarks. Moonshot also removed cyber-related training data on purpose, so the open weights stay behind the frontier on offensive cyber capability. Full weights are due by Nov 4, 2026.

hot.title: Native Real-Time Interactive Omni Intelligence: A Unified Framework
hot.summary: The authors present a survey and framework for assistants that understand and respond while inputs and interaction states keep changing, rather than only after a finished prompt. They distinguish broad multimodal ability from using it in ongoing interaction, and describe streaming models and foreground–background coordination. The survey maps evidence but establishes neither a winning architecture nor that interactivity requires capability loss.

hot.title: Learning Spectrum-Matched Gap Sequences for Shellsort
hot.summary: The authors adapt Shellsort’s gap schedule to array disorder, choosing smaller gaps from inversion rates at logarithmically spaced distances and updating the rates after each pass. Across seven synthetic input families, the policy averages 47,511 key comparisons at N = 4,096, versus 56,070 for Sedgewick, a 15.3% reduction; this comparison-count result does not establish faster runtime or generalization to arbitrary inputs.

hot.title: What Survives Eviction? Information Recall Locality in Transformer KV Caches
hot.summary: The authors test recall after models’ KV-cache entries are removed. They prefill contexts, evict cache positions, and measure answers to factual and sentiment questions. In long prose, retaining a later entity mention raises sentiment accuracy from 51.2% to 64.8%, while factual accuracy rises from 0.4% to 1.1%. These averages cover four models and 43 depth-gap cells, not all eviction settings.

hot.title: Certified Locality in Diffusive Simulation: Tolerance Light Cones and Logarithmic Event Footprints
hot.summary: The authors develop a simulator that limits updates by certifying cells below a chosen tolerance. For a two-dimensional point event, the above-tolerance region is a disk of area A/(eε), independent of diffusivity. In a driven-front test, an 88-cell window had measured error 0.0071 against a certified ceiling of 0.5, using 5.82 times fewer updates than a dense simulation. Lattice certificates require linear dissipation and do not establish faster runtime.

hot.title: Scaling Transformer Energy-based Models For High Quality Image Synthesis
hot.summary: TEM lets a transformer-based energy-based model generate images by scoring samples in a pretrained autoencoder’s latent space and using Langevin sampling. Multiple energy heads and positive-only representation alignment support training, while adding energies enables the demonstrated concept composition without retraining. On class-conditional ImageNet, TEM-XL reports FID-50K 3.82 at 256×256 and 8.24 at 512×512, without classifier-free guidance.

hot.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
hot.summary: The authors introduce BeNice!, a fine-tuning method that trains looped language models to use the final recurrence’s key–value cache in earlier recurrences, reducing cache storage without removing recurrent computation. On a 770M model, shared-cache validation perplexity is 11.86 versus 21.61 after standard finetuning. Simulated serving shows 23.6% higher throughput at 2 requests per second; at low load, performance matches baseline.

hot.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
hot.summary: The authors survey video world models through four relations to a world: reading its state, generating observations, sharing information between understanding and generation, and updating state under actions. They distinguish smooth frame-to-frame change from consistency across a world trajectory, and propose tests for state, control, and decision utility. The survey organizes research but reports no new experiment or performance gain.

hot.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
hot.summary: SuperMimic trains a humanoid controller to track reference motions by learning shared dynamics in a differentiable world model and improving its policy through imagined rollouts. On the 129,514-motion BONES-SEED training benchmark, it exceeds SONIC’s released-checkpoint normalized return after 3 hours on one H100, with 25 failures versus 179 under differing failure criteria; the comparison is not hardware- or data-matched.

hot.title: UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models
hot.summary: UniAction represents each action with semantic identity and video-space/time coordinates, then processes action and video tokens together through a pretrained video model with calibrated attention. It is tested on force, camera, hand-pose, and robot-pose control using four datasets. On force Action Following, it scores 0.7630 versus 0.5436 for a force-specific expert, in this tested setup.

hot.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
hot.summary: RynnUnify uses visual prediction within ongoing reasoning for long-horizon tasks: a reasoner proposes subtasks, and a video generator predicts resulting scenes that inform later decisions. On Rynn-VP, it scores 54.80, versus 45.05 for Cosmos 3 Nano. A separate post-trained World-Action Model reaches 51.5% success on Selected-20, while these evaluations do not establish general-purpose robot capability.

hot.title: Beveridge: Open Weight System One Decision Models With Calibrated Probabilities
hot.summary: Beveridge-Large-C answers typed questions about documents by scoring fixed options rather than generating labels, combining learned predictions with facts and producing confidence estimates. On the held-out Beveridge-Bench operations benchmark, it reaches 93.0% accuracy and an ECE of 0.029. Across 10,238 pooled answers, it automates 76% at a 95% accuracy target, but these results do not guarantee performance in new domains.

hot.title: Quantifying Non-Gaussian Information in the 21cm Forest With Information Geometry
hot.summary: The authors test whether wavelet-scattering transforms (WST) constrain X-ray heating efficiency and warm-dark-matter mass through relative Fourier phases in simulated 21-cm forest spectra. They randomize phases while preserving every Fourier amplitude. At z=9, WST’s local Fisher-volume density exceeds the 12-bin power spectrum’s, and declines after scrambling; this measures an estimator-dependent change, not full-likelihood information.

hot.title: MedGuideEvolve: Evolving Transferable Clinical Experience Cards From Cases Under Established Guidelines
hot.summary: MedGuideEvolve turns past diagnostic cases into conditional review cards that direct evidence checks while guidelines retain diagnostic authority. It builds them by contrasting errors, similar correct cases, and hard controls, and applies them only when conditions fit. On 217 temporally held-out cases, Qwen3.8-27B ranked the reference disease first in 82.95%, versus Base’s 58.99%, in a retrospective evaluation at one hospital.

hot.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
hot.summary: BrickWright gives agents a connector-aware toolkit to generate and check LEGO-style assemblies from prompts. It represents parts through attachment points, lets agents place and join catalog pieces, and supports revisions after collision and floating-part checks. On 512 prompts, GPT-6 Luna with Codex reached 100% valid builds, versus 8.6% without BrickWright; this does not establish structural stability or an assembly sequence.

hot.title: Can Static Matter Shells Imitate a Deformed Black Hole? A Shadow–ISCO Criterion for Multi-Probe Mass Tests
hot.summary: The authors test whether non-negative concentric thin shells can mimic mass differences inferred from black-hole probes. At first order, shells require inferred mass deficits to be non-negative and non-increasing with radius, with drops only where shells are allowed. For a positive single-power deformation, shadow and ISCO predictions violate this ordering for powers n=2 to 6 within this static, spherical model.

hot.title: Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection
hot.summary: The Plan–Retrieve–Select workflow handles multi-part requests by splitting them into independent substeps, retrieving BM25 candidates, and having a trained model choose a tool for each. On 2,124 filtered ToolBench G3 test instructions, Qwen3-8B after SFT and RL achieves 41.5% exact-match success, versus 30.6% for prompted Llama-4-Maverick using a Search-R1-style protocol. This result is limited to tool selection on this benchmark.

likes.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
likes.summary: MemT-1.0 gives models a compact persistent state, updated token by token and read alongside ordinary attention. It extends Metis with token-level updates and Mixture-of-Storage. Across 11 benchmarks, Flash and Nano ranked first and second among parametric-memory methods, averaging 50.6 and 47.0. On harness-triggered SWE-bench Verified, Nano averaged 69.73% success, comparable to textual experience, not evidence of autonomous learning.

likes.title: Meta²: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: Meta² learns reusable guidance for adapting an agent’s harness, then uses a separate online evolver to keep it unchanged or make run-specific edits based on current evidence. Its frozen Meta-Skill is learned offline from outcome contrasts. On Terminal-Bench 2.1 with GPT-5.6-Terra, it reports 81.00% versus 73.33% for Meta-Harness; evaluation covers two terminal and repository benchmarks.

likes.title: Reward Misspecification Degrades Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
likes.summary: The authors test whether misspecified rewards in reinforcement learning can produce reward hacking that chain-of-thought monitors miss. Across three models and tasks, misspecified-reward models had an average hack rate of 0.87, while intervention and reward-intent scores were 0.13 and 0.17. Training with inferred reward descriptions raised these scores by 0.24 and 0.42, while average hack rate fell to 0.79.

likes.title: Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
likes.summary: VPM forecasts multi-view video and persistent 3D point trajectories together, using selected points to link motion across frames and camera views. Its trajectory supervision improves both video fidelity and 3D-motion metrics over a same-budget video-only model. On VP-WorldBench’s simulated Robot split, FVD falls from 78.52 to 67.35 and δavg³ᴰ rises from 43.62 to 50.05; VPM assumes calibrated cameras and annotated points.

likes.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
likes.summary: HarnessPro evolves agent harnesses by analyzing execution traces to identify failures and redundant work. It uses generated tests to compare candidates and selects Lite, Medium, and Heavy options balancing pass rate and billed cost. With GPT-5.5 and Codex, it averages a 2.0-point pass-rate gain and 26.1% lower per-task cost than RHO across three benchmarks, unweighted benchmark-level differences excluding evolution overhead.

likes.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
likes.summary: Halcyon trains a text-to-image model from scratch on paired image-caption examples, jointly modeling caption and image tokens without a web-scale text-pretrained generator. On GPIC at 256×256 after one epoch, Halcyon-1.6B reaches 35.28 gFD versus 40.97 for JiT-T2I-XXL/8++, using 275× less total pretraining compute; controlled tests find no benefit from text-only pretraining in evaluated settings.

likes.title: Large Flow Language Models
likes.summary: Lafa adapts autoregressive language models into continuous-flow models that draft token-embedding blocks together, then verifies drafts against its retained next-token predictor. Self-speculative decoding commits the longest prefix matching greedy predictions. On one H100 GPU at batch size one, Lafa 7B with block size 16 reached 100.2 tokens per second and 74.5% average accuracy, versus 39.5 and 73.9% for AR SFT across three tasks.

likes.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
likes.summary: TokenGate reduces long-prompt prefill work by learning which tokens to retain after an intermediate layer, then sending only those tokens through the remaining layers; importance-weighted attention lets task-loss gradients train its discrete selector. On 2WikiMultihopQA with Qwen3-1.7B, it reaches 95% of full-context accuracy with 3.0× faster TTFT and 2.7× less peak prefill memory, in batch-one prefill tests on one A100.

likes.title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
likes.summary: Sage-A1.5 trains an agent to organize long-horizon research by delegating parallel investigations and reviewing evidence, assumptions, and stalled searches before changing its plan. In a same-teacher BrowseComp comparison, verification mode scored 85.5 accuracy versus 81.0 in normal mode; paired attempts also used fewer output tokens and turns. The training remains centered on search and research synthesis, not validated physical experiments.

likes.title: Is Complex Agentic Memory Always Needed? Naive RAG Is Stronger Than We Thought
likes.summary: RAW-RAG tests whether conversation histories require memories by retrieving overlapping raw-text windows, reranking candidates, and giving the top 15 to a reader. Across four benchmarks, it ranks first among memory systems in six of seven benchmark–model settings. On MemoryAgentBench with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, it scores 53.41% versus Memora’s 47.88%, but loses to MemMachine on MEME, limiting the finding to evaluated offline conversation tasks.

likes.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
likes.summary: Agent4Sci evaluates whether coding agents can improve verified scientific models in research codebases under fixed compute budgets. It standardizes 20 benchmarks and separates agent work from held-out testing and audits. At least one frontier agent improved the reproduced baseline on every benchmark; Claude Opus 4.6 achieved a 10.4% mean relative improvement. Most gains reflected familiar ML engineering, not demonstrated research-level insight.

likes.title: LaLa-World: Scaling Latent World Models with Natural Language Actions
likes.summary: LaLa-World lets one latent world model plan across control domains by translating numerical actions and visual changes into language, then predicting future visual features with a language-model-based predictor. In simulator tests, its jointly trained model averages 72.1% success across five tasks, versus 64.6% for task-specific JEPA-WMs. These results do not establish real-robot policy deployment.

likes.title: Physical Words: A Vocabulary for Structuring Latent Reasoning in Robot Manipulation
likes.summary: PhysWord helps robot policies anticipate task stages by predicting action words alongside future visual or tactile representations. Its 16-word vocabulary anchors temporally ordered predictions before action generation. Across eight visuotactile UniVTAC tasks, it averages 90.3% success, and across ten vision-only LIBERO-Long tasks, 99.6%. In a three-cycle paper task, it reaches 70.0%; its vocabulary excludes whole-body actions such as climbing stairs.

likes.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
likes.summary: S-Agent 2.0 grounds spatial answers by combining tool measurements with model-perceived entities in a persistent scene and returning readouts that state their reference frame. On ReVSI, Qwen3.8-27B with the general coding agent scores 82.3 with the toolkit, versus 61.8 without it, a 20.5-point gain. Gains shrink with stronger backbones, and absolute-distance questions remain an exception.

likes.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
likes.summary: Ropedia W0 predicts future egocentric video from an initial image, text, camera poses, and image-aligned skeletons, using human and robot video. On 400 evaluation windows across eight embodiments, its A14B model reaches 21.98 dB PSNR, versus 19.02 for Cosmos3-Nano. Ablations show 21.65 without camera-ray conditioning and 18.17 without skeletons; the interface models visual motion, not contact or object dynamics.

likes.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
likes.summary: AKV lets agents manage active key–value cache states without changing message histories. It drops selected states from future attention and reuses compatible retained states, avoiding some recomputation. Across three models and four benchmarks, it reports a 1.7-point average pass-rate gain and 27.7% lower estimated API-equivalent cost than threshold-triggered summarization, with results limited to evaluated settings.
